claim: Base UI became the default primitive layer in shadcn/ui in July 2026; Radix is not deprecated and remains available via the -b radix flag; new projects pick Base UI over Radix 2:1.
quote: Starting today, Base UI is the default component library in shadcn/ui. ... Radix is not being deprecated. We still support it, and every update and new component will ship for both libraries. ... Projects created on shadcn/create now pick Base UI over Radix 2 to 1.

claim: Base UI 1.0 shipped Dec 11 2025 with 35 accessible components, built by engineers from Radix, Floating UI and Material UI; maintainers reject the 'Radix successor' framing; package renamed to @base-ui/react.
quote: The components handle complex interaction patterns, keyboard navigation, focus management, and ARIA attributes, ensuring WCAG compliance out of the box. ... It's to communicate that it's easy to migrate from Radix to Base UI due to the API similarity. ... Base UI is supported by MUI, a company with engineers, designers, and managers dedicated to the project.

claim: Base UI repo: 10,335 stars, 7 open accessibility-labelled issues, actively pushed July 2026.
quote: Unstyled UI components for building accessible web apps and design systems.

claim: Radix Primitives is still maintained by WorkOS; 19,064 stars, repo pushed 13 Jul 2026, ~10 open accessibility-titled issues.
quote: Radix Primitives is an open-source UI component library for building high-quality, accessible design systems and web apps. Maintained by @workos.

claim: shadcn/ui repo: 119,064 stars; 6 open accessibility-titled issues.
quote: A set of beautifully-designed, accessible components and a code distribution platform.

claim: Mantine repo: 31,424 stars, only 35 open issues total and 0 open accessibility-titled issues.
quote: A fully featured React components library

claim: React Spectrum / React Aria repo: 15,662 stars, 33 open accessibility-labelled issues.
quote: A collection of libraries and tools that help you build adaptive, accessible, and robust user experiences.

claim: Ark UI repo: 5,282 stars, 12 open issues total.
quote: Unstyled, accessible UI components for your design System. Works in React, Vue, Solid, and Svelte.

claim: Material UI repo: 98,582 stars and 88 open accessibility-labelled issues — the largest a11y backlog of the kits compared.
quote: Material UI: Comprehensive React component library that implements Google's Material Design.

claim: React Aria publishes a named screen-reader test matrix (VoiceOver macOS/iOS, JAWS, NVDA, TalkBack) but claims no WCAG conformance level and publishes no VPAT.
quote: React Aria components are tested across a wide variety of devices, browsers, and screen readers. ... Automated accessibility testing tools sometimes catch false positives in React Aria.

claim: Mantine tests interactive components with jest-axe and manually with VoiceOver only; explicitly disclaims full app-level accessibility.
quote: All components that have interactive elements are tested with axe (jest-axe) ... Mantine components are manually tested with screen readers (VoiceOver) ... While Mantine components provide a solid foundation for accessible applications, there are still things that you need to do.

claim: Base UI claims WAI-ARIA APG adherence and automatic focus management, and unspecified 'broad spectrum' screen-reader testing, but names no test matrix and claims no WCAG level.
quote: Base UI components adhere to the WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices to provide basic keyboard accessibility out of the box. ... Base UI components manage focus automatically following a user interaction. ... tested on a broad spectrum of browsers, devices, platforms, screen readers, and environments.

claim: The request for MUI ADA/WCAG compliance documentation has been open since January 2019 with no maintainer position and no VPAT produced.
quote: [all components][docs] Create ADA compliance documentation — labels: accessibility/a11y, docs, scope: all components; status: open (filed 15 Jan 2019).

claim: Independent 2026 comparison calls React Aria the most accessibility-rigorous headless library, and notes Radix updates have slowed for complex components while Base UI iterates faster.
quote: the most accessibility-rigorous option in this list ... Radix UI was acquired by WorkOS and updates have slowed for some complex components ... maintained by MUI with full-time engineers.

claim: A 2026 audit (VoiceOver/Safari, NVDA/Firefox, axe DevTools, Lighthouse, WAVE) found 34/48 shadcn components pass WCAG 2.2 AA, 9 need minor fixes, 5 have real gaps; the default focus ring measures 2.4:1, below the 3:1 non-text contrast threshold.
quote: The default Button uses focus-visible:ring-ring/50 which renders the focus indicator at 50% opacity. In light mode against a white background, the resulting contrast ratio is 2.4:1 — below the WCAG AA threshold of 3:1 for non-text contrast.

claim: MUI's 2026 roadmap: Base UI is the major focus; new components (NumberField, MenuBar, PreviewCard) are built on Base UI, but Material UI is not being rebuilt on top of it.
quote: Base UI is a major area of focus in 2026, with efforts on expanding the component set, improving documentation and guidance, and making adoption and migration easier for teams building their custom design systems.

claim: Radix has a named active maintainer, Chance Strickland, employed by WorkOS (Nov 2025).
quote: Chance Strickland is a software engineer at WorkOS and a maintainer of Radix UI.

claim: Radix is actively released in 2026: radix-ui 1.6.2 published 6 Jul 2026 with 1.6.3 release candidates through 13 Jul 2026; ~10.2M weekly downloads for the meta package and 66.8M for @radix-ui/react-dialog.
react-aria has ~7.4M weekly npm downloads (Jul 2026).
quote: last-week downloads: 7,425,270 (npm downloads API).

claim: @base-ui/react is at 1.6.0 (published 18 Jun 2026) with ~6.2M weekly downloads; the legacy @base-ui-components/react package has collapsed to ~0.4M.
quote: latest 1.6.0 — 2026-06-18T12:04:15Z; last-week downloads: 6,195,828.

claim: @mui/material 9.2.0 depends on Popper, react-transition-group, @mui/system and @mui/utils — no Base UI and no Radix, confirming MUI Core implements its own accessibility behaviour; ~7.8M weekly downloads.
quote: dependencies: @babel/runtime, @popperjs/core, @types/react-transition-group, clsx, csstype, prop-types, react-is, react-transition-group, @mui/core-downloads-tracker, @mui/types, @mui/system, @mui/utils.

claim: @mantine/core 9.4.1 depends only on @floating-ui/react, clsx, react-number-format, react-remove-scroll and type-fest — all widget behaviour and ARIA wiring is self-implemented; ~1.6M weekly downloads.
quote: dependencies: @floating-ui/react ^0.27.19, clsx ^2.1.1, react-number-format ^5.4.5, react-remove-scroll ^2.7.2, type-fest ^5.7.0.

claim: Publicis Sapient's Accessibility Center of Excellence audited Radix across VoiceOver/Safari (macOS+iOS), NVDA/Firefox and TalkBack/Chrome, found 35 accessibility issues, and the tracking issue filed Aug 2023 is still open.
quote: Members of Publicis Sapient's Accessibility Center of Excellence performed the audit ... identified 35 accessibility issues ... we are really eager to help if possible.

claim: Ark UI provides 40+ headless components across React/Vue/Solid/Svelte, every component backed by a Zag.js finite state machine; ~0.93M weekly npm downloads.
quote: Ark UI is built on top of Zag.js, a UI component library powered by Finite State Machines. ... more than 40+ components and tools to help you build accessible, complex, and feature-rich UI design systems.

claim: MUI states WCAG Level AA as an aspiration ('what we aim to support'), per-component, rather than a conformance claim.
quote: Level AA exceeds the basic criteria for accessibility and is a common target for most organizations, so this is what we aim to support.

claim: shadcn shipped full Base UI documentation in January 2026 and rebuilt every component example for both Radix and Base UI before making Base UI the default in July.
quote: December brought npx shadcn create with both libraries. January brought full Base UI docs.
